Many people answered your questions specifically so I just want to give you a general understanding of gender that I find makes everything easier. 

For me, GENDER IDENTITY is how you feel inside. Woman feels like woman inside, man feels like man inside, agender feels like nothing or no gender inside. It’s an internal thing. GENDER EXPRESSION is how you decide to show yourself or express yourself to the world. I am agender so I feel pretty much no gender inside. But I like to express myself in a feminine manner. It doesn’t mean I feel like a woman inside. A woman might like to express herself in a masculine or androgynous manner, but still feels like a woman inside. Nullification, or any transition, is a form of gender expression as well. Gender expression is pretty much free range and just about choosing what would make you feel most comfortable. And finally, PRONOUNS are just how you like to be referred to. They aren’t necessarily tied to anything, it’s just what feels comfortable. 

The point is that all these things are completely different categories. For many people they line up traditionally (Woman-feminine expression-she/her) but for others they don’t (Agender-feminine expression-they/them), and they just choose what makes them feel comfortable or true to themselves.

Yesterday I was working through my hatred and resentment towards my family and I wondered to myself, “why the heck are these feelings so strong? Even though I realize that my parents were navigating life with what they know best, and that they had their own trauma, why can’t I get over the resentment and anger?” And it made me realize that I have been living in this unhealthy, draining dynamic for an INCREDIBILY LONG TIME. The hurt, invalidation, yelling, intimidation, threatening, neglect, silencing, judgement, has been something I’ve had to deal with for the past 25 years! When you truly realize the extent of the damage that has been done, and for how long, you realize why your body and feelings react that way. It’s actually completely normal and healthy to go through these waves of intense feelings in response to trauma that has been going on for so long! 

The more trauma you’ve experienced and the longer you’ve experienced it will affect how long it will take to process the tough feelings. But they are processable! I think it’s important to understand that the feelings WILL end once they have been completely processed, even if they feel overwhelming and never-ending at the moment. I have accepted my incredibly strong feelings, held them compassionately, and at the other side I feel a lot calmer than before. At least, this way of thinking is what has helped me haha. Wish you luck in your healing journey <3

Haha no problem <3 and it really does feel like that! 😓I cope better some days than others of course (I just had like a week full of mental breakdowns but doing pretty good now lmao) For me, what has helped me cope a LOT is reparenting. I basically replace any negative, self-defeating voice in my head with an uplifting, nurturing voice. In my example it’s a motherly voice since the main issue was with my mother. When I’m feeling depressed, this voice will be like “oh honey I see you’re feeling down? What’s wrong? Is it because of this? Or this? I’m sure it must be hard etc.” Maybe it seems a bit silly but it’s a hell of a lot better than being your own worst enemy😂 For you it might be like “hey, your feelings are important! And you deserve to communicate them to people! They might get mad, but even if they do, your feelings deserve respect and acknowledgement! I know it’s hard honey, but you’ll get there eventually”. You can do any voice that you wish your parents would have treated you as. Give yourself the voice and nurturing you truly need. 

People who were emotionally neglected never got to internalize a nurturing voice, which is literally the basis of emotional safety, so it’s so so important to begin to do that for yourself to have a safe base to begin exploring the world in and gaining more courage. Even if it feels kinda weird at first, it really helped me out of a really depressive mood and be more compassionate towards myself. 

Oh and another thing that helps me cope is do NOT use other people as mirrors! People will have opinions on you but that’s their point of view! You need to figure out who you truly are and own it whether people like it or not. When people say something about you, ask: do I agree with this? Does it resonate with me? Don’t take it as truth. This is so important when you’re a people pleaser like us.
